note: A numeric cell may carry a currency symbol, source-grouped or split digits, decimals, parentheses, percent, multiple, or basis-point suffix; punctuation-only strings do not qualify.
A detached printed unit joins the numeric word immediately to its left when the coordinate gap also qualifies.
A four-digit calendar year can name a column or complete a printed period label.
A small parenthesized number beside a header is a footnote marker rather than a data value.
A one- or two-digit token may complete a period header such as 9 Months or 10 Year.
Only a printed period label permits an all-year first value column to fold into that label.
Currency decimal percentage and parenthesis marks distinguish a printed data value from a bare year header.
